summary: Adds email search to the users index, adds update and destroy endpoints with routes, and sends a welcome email from a User save callback.

findings.title: Search term interpolated into SQL
findings.problem: The index action puts params[:q] directly into the SQL text of the where clause. Nothing escapes or binds the value.
findings.consequence: Any authenticated caller can inject SQL and read or change any table, including api tokens. The caller can also break the query.
findings.fix: Pass the search term as a bound parameter and escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.title: Destroy action skips the admin check
findings.problem: The change adds destroy to the require_admin exception list. The destroy action then deletes any user by id with no ownership or role check.
findings.consequence: Any authenticated user can delete every other user, including admins. This causes data loss.
findings.fix: Keep destroy behind require_admin, or scope the lookup to the current user.

findings.title: Welcome email sent on every save
findings.problem: The after_save callback runs on create and on every update. The new update action and any other save trigger it again.
findings.consequence: Users receive a new welcome email each time an admin or the code updates their record. The job may also run before the transaction commits.
findings.fix: Use after_create_commit so the email goes out once, after the record is committed.

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds search, update, destroy and a mail callback. The repository has no test that exercises any of them.
findings.consequence: Regressions in authorization and the email callback can ship unnoticed. Reviewers cannot confirm the intended behaviour.
findings.fix: Add request tests for search, update and destroy, and a model test for the welcome email callback.

dropped.reason: The update action stays behind require_admin, so only admins reach this lookup. An admin may update any user by design.
